title: Killing Bites
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: College student Yuya Nomoto is pulled into the Killing Bites, secret death matches between human-animal hybrids ('Brutes') that powerful zaibatsu bet on to settle economic power. He becomes the backer of Hitomi, a fearless honey badger hybrid, and after a later betrayal by her guardian Shido he turns to revenge against Shido and the zaibatsu.
life_message: Strength, nerve and cunning decide who survives in a world where the powerful treat living beings as weapons.

content.note: Lethal hybrid death matches and killings from the first chapter; AniList Gore tag and MU Blood and Gore agree with Wikipedia plot.
Kill-or-be-killed tournaments, monstrous transformations, a berserk experimental hybrid (Wikipedia, MU).

Taunting is Hitomi's fighting style (Wikipedia); profanity level not documented (to verify).

Manipulation of Hitomi through her crush on Shido; no self-harm reported.
Kidnapping attempt in chapter one and revenge plotting; superhuman fights are not easily copied.
Anime adaptation exists; no product tie-ins in the story.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Hitomi provokes opponents with insults; fights and grudges (Eruza's vengeance on Ui) settle standing personally.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Underground matches outside law; Yuya lives among hybrids after being declared dead.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty runs to one's zaibatsu, guardian or small band, not society at large.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Zaibatsu hierarchy is real but cast as corrupt; heroes fight against it.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Genetic science drives the world; matches claimed as ancient custom but serve economic power.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Kill-or-be-killed survival and strength dominate the story's values.

folkways.japan: The four zaibatsu echo Japan's historic family-run business conglomerates, used here as shadowy power blocs.

delivery.evidence: Sources describe action and plot, not speeches; no reviewer comment on messaging found (to verify).
delivery.note: The story carries its view of power through fights and betrayals rather than through stated arguments.

winners_losers: Fearless fighters and those who outwit the zaibatsu gain sympathy; the manipulative Shido and the greedy zaibatsu are the targets of Yuya's revenge.
